relations.definition: The organization or entity responsible for monitoring and reporting a particular index or metric
relations.embedding_query_text: tracked_by: The organization or entity responsible for monitoring and reporting a particular index or metric

instances: US wholesale inflation slowed in July -> Bureau of Labor Statistics

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: sdPublisher
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for generating and publishing the structured data markup for a creative work. Also called structured data provider, metadata publisher, data markup creator. Examples: `Article Structured Data` sdPublisher `Schema.org Generator`, `Open Data Project` sdPublisher `University Research Group`, `Student Project` sdPublisher `Jane Doe`. Distinct from `publisher`, which is the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: trackingUrl
candidates.comment: A tracking URL relation between a parcel delivery and the web address for monitoring its status. Also called shipment tracking link, parcel status URL, delivery tracking page. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://example.com/track/12345'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://shipper.com/status?id=ABCDE'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://delivery.com/track/FGHIJ'".

candidates.label: trackingNumber
candidates.comment: A tracking number relation between a parcel delivery and its unique identifier provided by the shipper. Also called shipment ID, parcel ID, delivery tracking code. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '1Z999AA10123456784'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber 'JD0001234567890123'", "ParcelDelivery trackingNumber '9400100000000000000000'".

candidates.label: measurementMethod
candidates.comment: A measurement method relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the specific method used for measurement. Also called: method of measurement, specific technique, measurement approach. Examples: "Temperature Dataset measurementMethod 'Thermocouple'", "Survey Data measurementMethod 'Likert Scale'", "Chemical Analysis measurementMethod 'Spectrophotometry'". Distinct from measurementTechnique, which is a broader property that measurementMethod is a subproperty of.

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The about property aligns with the relation to economic indices and price specifications.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: step
candidates.comment: A component relation between a how-to guide and a single instruction, section, or creative work that forms part of the process. Also called "instructional step", "how-to instruction", "process step", "guide step". Examples: "The recipe has step 'Chop vegetables'", "The guide's step is a video tutorial", "This how-to includes a step for assembly.". Distinct from steps, which refers to a collection of steps.

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate
candidates.comment: A coinsurance rate relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and the numerical rate of coinsurance. Also called coinsurance percentage, rate of coinsurance, coinsurance ratio. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance rate of 0.2.", "The specification includes a coinsurance rate of 0.15.", "This plan's coinsurance rate is 0.3."

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: sensoryUnit
candidates.comment: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. Examples: `Optic Nerve` sensoryUnit `Retina`, `Auditory Nerve` sensoryUnit `Cochlea`, `Median Nerve` sensoryUnit `Skin of Hand`. Distinct from `motorUnit`, which transmits motor commands.

candidates.label: loanMortgageMandateAmount
candidates.comment: A mortgage mandate amount relation between a mortgage loan and the monetary amount that can be converted into a mortgage. Also called: mortgage potential, convertible mortgage amount, mandate value. Examples: "Home Loan loanMortgageMandateAmount $200,000", "Property Mortgage loanMortgageMandateAmount €150,000", "Commercial Loan loanMortgageMandateAmount £500,000".

candidates.label: numberOfBathroomsTotal
candidates.comment: The total integer count of all bathrooms (full, three-quarter, and half) within an accommodation or floor plan. Also called total bathroom count, bathroom total, sum of bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBathroomsTotal 2", "House B numberOfBathroomsTotal 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfBathroomsTotal 1". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms and numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specify specific types of bathrooms.

candidates.label: eligibleDuration
candidates.comment: An eligible duration relation between a demand or offer and the quantitative value representing the period for which it is valid. Also called "validity period", "offer duration", "term length". Examples: "Offer 'Limited Time Sale' eligibleDuration 'P7D'", "Subscription offer eligibleDuration 'P1Y'", "Demand 'Project Bid' eligibleDuration 'P30D'".

candidates.label: suitableForDiet
candidates.comment: An indication of a dietary restriction or guideline for which a recipe or menu item is appropriate. Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."

candidates.label: drugUnit
candidates.comment: A drug unit relation between a drug or drug cost and the text describing the unit in which the drug is measured. Also called "medication unit", "dosage unit". Examples: "Drug 'Aspirin' drugUnit '500 mg tablet'", "Drug cost drugUnit 'per vial'", "Drug 'Insulin' drugUnit 'units'".

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: educationalRole
candidates.comment: An educational role relation between an educational audience and the text describing its specific role. Also called "audience role", "learner role", "student type". Examples: "Educational audience educationalRole 'Student'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Teacher'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Parent'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byMonthWeek
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the week(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "week of month", "monthly week recurrence", "on week of month". Examples: "Book club schedule byMonthWeek 2", "Team sync schedule byMonthWeek 1,3".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasCourseInstance
candidates.comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. Examples: "A calculus course has a course instance for Fall 2023.", "The online course has a course instance for self-paced study.", "A cooking class has a course instance on Tuesdays at 6 PM."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: A merchant return policy relation between an offer, organization, or product and its applicable return policy. Also called return policy, refund policy, returns information. Examples: "A product has a merchant return policy of 30 days.", "An organization has a merchant return policy for all sales.", "The offer includes a merchant return policy."

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

relations.definition: A component or subset of a larger whole
relations.embedding_query_text: part_of: A component or subset of a larger whole

instances: Core PPI rose 0.2% in July -> US wholesale inflation slowed in July

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

relations.definition: A statement or claim that is credited to a specific individual or entity
relations.embedding_query_text: attributed_to: A statement or claim that is credited to a specific individual or entity

instances: Fuel prices remain wild card due to Iran conflict -> Ben Ayers

chosen_property.label: creditedTo
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a performance assessment and the person responsible for it.

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: creditText
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a creative work and the text used to credit associated persons or organizations. Also called: attribution text, credit line, acknowledgment. Examples: "Movie" credit text "Directed by...", "Photograph" credit text "Photo by John Doe", "Research Paper" credit text "Funding provided by...". Distinct from creator, which identifies the primary author/creator.

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: sameAs
candidates.comment: A URL that identifies the same real-world entity as the item, providing an unambiguous reference to its identity. Also called equivalent to, identical to, linked identity, canonical URL. Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for the item, not necessarily an identity link.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."

candidates.label: relatedDrug
candidates.comment: A related drug relation between a drug and other drugs that are similar or commonly prescribed alternatives. Also called alternative drug, similar medication, related medication. Examples: "A pain reliever has a related drug 'ibuprofen'.", "An antidepressant has a related drug 'SSRI'.", "A blood pressure medication has a related drug 'diuretic'."

candidates.label: relatedTherapy
candidates.comment: A related therapy relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical therapy associated with it. Also called associated therapy, treatment for. Examples: "The knee joint has a related therapy 'physical therapy'.", "The respiratory system has a related therapy 'inhaler treatment'.", "The skin has a related therapy 'topical cream application'."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

relations.definition: An event or factor that leads to a specific outcome or effect
relations.embedding_query_text: caused_by: An event or factor that leads to a specific outcome or effect

instances: Wholesale inflation cooling after Iran war spike -> Iran war
Semiconductor prices up 27.1% annually -> AI build-out

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: interactingDrug
candidates.comment: A drug interaction relation between two drugs, where one affects the action or safety of the other. Also called drug-drug interaction, co-administered drug, reactive drug. Examples: Warfarin has an interactingDrug of 'Aspirin'. Antibiotics have an interactingDrug of 'Oral contraceptives'. Statins have an interactingDrug of 'Grapefruit juice'. Distinct from contraindication, which typically refers to a disease or condition that makes a drug unsuitable.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

instances: AI build-out -> data centers

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: driveWheelConfiguration
candidates.comment: A drive wheel configuration relation between a vehicle and the value or text describing which roadwheels receive torque from the engine. Also called "drivetrain type", "wheel drive system". Examples: "Car 'SUV' driveWheelConfiguration 'AllWheelDriveConfiguration'", "Truck driveWheelConfiguration '4x4'", "Sedan driveWheelConfiguration 'FrontWheelDriveConfiguration'".

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorType
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior type relation between a vehicle and the type or material of its interior. Also called interior material, upholstery type, cabin trim. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'synthetic fabric'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'wood trim'".

candidates.label: vehicleSeatingCapacity
candidates.comment: A vehicle seating capacity relation between a vehicle and the number of passengers it can seat. Also called seating capacity, passenger capacity, number of seats. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '5'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '7 persons'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '2'".

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: vehicleIdentificationNumber
candidates.comment: A vehicle identification number relation between a vehicle and its unique serial number (VIN). Also called VIN, chassis number, serial number. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleIdentificationNumber '1G1AP52W691XXXXXX'", "Car vehicleIdentificationNumber 'JTDKN31V60JXXXXXX'", "Truck vehicleIdentificationNumber '3FAHP000000XXXXXX'".

Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: inverseOf

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: followup
candidates.comment: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: honorificSuffix
candidates.comment: An honorific suffix relation between a person and a title following their name. Also called post-nominal title, suffix title, academic suffix. Examples: "A person has an honorific suffix 'PhD'.", "His honorific suffix is 'M.D.'.", "The individual uses the honorific suffix 'Jr.'."

candidates.label: exerciseRelatedDiet
candidates.comment: An exercise-related diet relation between an exercise action and the diet followed in conjunction with that action. Also called: workout diet, fitness diet, training nutrition. Examples: "Marathon Training" exercise related diet "High-Carb Diet", "Bodybuilding Workout" exercise related diet "High-Protein Diet", "Weight Loss Program" exercise related diet "Calorie-Restricted Diet".

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.
